Riechman and colleagues (68) reported that a polymorphism in the IL-15 gene explained a significant proportion of the hypertrophic variation in a group of 153 young men and women following 10 weeks of heavy resistance training. These findings are supported by a recent study showing an upregulation of IL-15R α (a receptor that regulates IL-15 signaling) gene expression after resistance exercise, with a positive correlation ( r = .66) seen between elevations and increases in myofibrillar protein synthesis (58).
